subject: CareLattice: PO mandate + invoice rhythm impacting discount tiers
messages:
From: Samantha O'Neill <samantha.oneill@carelattice.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@carelattice.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: PO formatting and invoice cadence for upcoming contract

Vanessa —

Thanks for the proposal draft. Procurement had a quick review and we have two firm requirements before we can accept any discount terms: 1) A PO number must appear on every invoice as a header field (our ERP requires PO on line 1), and 2) invoices must land on the last business day of each month to align with our month-end close.

Separately, our treasury team prefers net45 payment terms, but we can consider net30 for certain early-pay discounts. Can you confirm whether your billing team can: a) include the PO in the invoice header, b) issue monthly invoices on the last business day, and c) offer a tiered discount depending on cadence/terms (monthly net45 vs monthly net30 vs quarterly prepay)?

I've attached our standard PO template for reference.

Attachment: CareLattice_PO_Template.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

— Samantha O'Neill
Director, Strategic Sourcing
CareLattice
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Samantha O'Neill <samantha.oneill@carelattice.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Procurement Team <procurement@carelattice.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO formatting and invoice cadence for upcoming contract

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear requirements and the PO template, that helps a lot. Short answers: yes on PO in the header, and yes we can schedule invoices to hit the last business day of the month.

A few notes on how the cadence intersects with discounts so your treasury team can decide:
- Monthly invoices on the last business day + net45: we can offer a 6% volume discount on committed usage tiers (applies to base subscription and overages).
- Monthly invoices on last business day + net30: we can offer 7% (we typically reserve ~1% premium for earlier payment).
- Quarterly prepay (billed at start of quarter): we can provide 9% and an onboarding credit if paid upfront.

Operationally, our billing system can include the exact PO field in the PDF header and populate your PO id into our invoice metadata for ERP matching. For milestone/usage billing (if you want partial invoices for milestone-enabled line items) we recommend mapping those line items to separate PO lines in your template — we can support that mapping.

I've copied Marissa (Revenue Ops) to confirm any necessary ledger tagging and to Ben (Finance) for cash application notes. I'll attach the current SOW we discussed so legal has a starting point.

Attachment: RI_SOW_v3.docx

Next step: if Procurement is comfortable with net45 + 6% for monthly-as-requested, confirm in reply and we will issue a commercial redline and send to your legal team. If you prefer to push to net30 we can adjust the discount to 7% on signature.

Best —
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Samantha O'Neill <samantha.oneill@carelattice.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-07T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO formatting and invoice cadence for upcoming contract

Samantha — quick technical note from Sales Ops + Finance:

1) PO header: we will add a dedicated "PO Number:" field on the invoice PDF and push the same value to the EDI/ERP metadata feed. That ensures your AP system can auto-match.
2) Last-business-day scheduling: our billing run for contracted customers can be scheduled to the last business day; we'll flag the invoices to use the month-of-service date range but invoice date as the last business day to match your close.
3) Discount calculation: discounts are applied at invoice generation time, not retroactively, so we need to confirm committed tiers up front. For customers who use variable usage, we can include a true-up process at quarter-end.

Marissa — please confirm the ledger tag schema we should expose to CareLattice so their AP can map to BU codes. Ben — FYI on net45 vs net30 cash application expectations (we may need to flag the receivable aging bucket differently).

If Procurement wants partial milestone invoices, we can emulate that by issuing interim invoices tied to named PO line items; however, that will split revenue recognition and could affect the discount eligibility if the volume threshold isn't met within the quarter.

Happy to discuss on a 20-min call if helpful.

— Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Samantha O'Neill <samantha.oneill@carelattice.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@carelattice.com>, Tony Ruiz <tony.ruiz@carelattice.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO formatting and invoice cadence for upcoming contract

Vanessa / Karthik —

Appreciate the quick follow-ups and the clarity. A couple of clarifications from our end after we chatted with treasury/ERP:
- The PO number must be the first visible field in the invoice PDF (ERP requires that for automated matching).
- Our month-end close is strict: invoices must be dated the last business day of the month and post to our AP ledger on that date.
- For usage-based charges we prefer a consolidated monthly invoice instead of separate milestone invoices. If you do interim milestone invoices we'll need a single monthly statement that consolidates all interim invoices for matching.

Given that, Procurement is willing to accept the monthly-last-business-day approach with net45. For now reconciliation team prefers the 6% discount option you listed. We will get legal to review your SOW and will send the signed PO template back with our PO number once legal finishes the redlines.

Attachment: CareLattice_PO_Template.pdf (updated)

Samantha
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Samantha O'Neill <samantha.oneill@carelattice.com>, Tony Ruiz <tony.ruiz@carelattice.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-10T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO formatting and invoice cadence for upcoming contract

Thanks Samantha — this is great and aligns with what we can do. To summarize and lock it in: 
- Invoice header will show "PO Number: XXXXXX" as the first visible field in the invoice PDF.
- Invoices will be generated with an invoice date on the last business day of the month and will include a monthly consolidated statement that lists all line items (including any interim milestone invoices) for easy ERP matching.
- Pricing: 6% discount for agreed committed tiers, applied on each monthly invoice, net45.

Next steps for us: 1) we will send a commercial redline to your legal team this afternoon, 2) Finance will prepare onboarding docs for PO mapping, and 3) once we receive the signed PO with the PO number we will schedule the first invoice to land on the next month-end.

Tony / Procurement: can you confirm your legal point-of-contact for SOW redlines so we route the doc correctly?

Thanks everyone — looks like we're close.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Tony Ruiz <tony.ruiz@carelattice.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, Samantha O'Neill <samantha.oneill@carelattice.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@carelattice.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO formatting and invoice cadence for upcoming contract

Vanessa / Team —

Confirming Procurement is okay with the plan: last-business-day monthly invoices with "PO Number" in the top header and net45 payment terms. CareLattice will accept the 6% discount for committed tiers as discussed. Our legal will take a look at the SOW and we will return a signed PO (using the attached template) with the PO number populated.

Please route the commercial redline to legal@carelattice.com and cc procurement@carelattice.com. Once legal signs, we'll provide the PO number and target the first invoice for 2026-09-30 (month of service: Sept).

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

— Tony Ruiz
Sr. Manager, Procurement
CareLattice
Attachment: CareLattice_PO_Template.pdf (signed placeholder)
